Alex W: FYI AcmePay reported a sudden burst of 429s hitting our API around 09:14 UTC. They say requests to /v1/generate are getting throttled even though they didn't change code.
Maya (support): Can you paste their request IDs or a sample header? We need to know if it's quota exhaustion vs spike protection.
AcmePay Admin: here are two request IDs: req_01G6Q7D8A9 and req_01G6Q7D8B0. We see X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 in the response and the body says "quota exceeded". We were doing a batch re-score job (same model) for 15 minutes.
Jake (SRE): grabbing logs now. Looks like a classic burst that exceeded per-minute bursts on our shared route. I see their client_id: acct-acmepay and route: /v1/generate. Model: gptx-13b-quant (variant: q4_0).
Jake (SRE): logs snippet:
```
[2026-04-02T09:14:23Z] client=acct-acmepay route=/v1/generate model=gptx-13b-quant status=429 reason=rate_limited remaining=0 limit=120 window=60
[2026-04-02T09:14:24Z] client=acct-acmepay route=/v1/generate status=429 trace=req_01G6Q7D8A9
```
Maya (support): thank you. Is this hitting the per-customer quota or the shared route-level burst guard? Which metric to check in console?
Jake (SRE): two things to check in dashboards: 1) quota-usage-by-customer panel (time series of tokens/sec and 1m rolling counts) 2) burst-events table (shows envelope of bursts and which guard fired). On our side the guard is "route_burst_guard_v2".
Maya (support): link to dashboard for quick reference: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/dashboards/limits?panel=quota-usage-by-customer (internal)
Alex W: Acme says they're on the Pro plan with burst allowance 2x base for scheduled jobs. Billing Ops, can you confirm quota config for acct-acmepay?
Billing Ops: confirmed. Pro plan: base RPS token cap 2,000 tokens/min with burst bucket +2,000 for 5 minutes. Their usage is occasionally higher because they parallelize 20 workers.
Jake (SRE): instrumentation shows tokens_emitted label by client and route. For attribution look at metric: redwood.requests.tokens_emitted{client_id="acct-acmepay",route="/v1/generate",model="gptx-13b-quant"}. Also check alerts: rate_limit_alerts_total{severity="throttle",guard="route_burst_guard_v2"}.
Maya (support): how do we explain the 429s to the customer? They want clear repro steps and a fix.
Jake (SRE): repro steps we documented: 1) reproduce locally by running 20 concurrent clients sending 3s prompt windows with model gptx-13b-quant 2) observe X-RateLimit-* headers drop to 0 3) confirm error body contains "quota exceeded". I'll paste a curl example: 
```
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-quant","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":256}' &
done
```
Maya (support): good. Any quick mitigation for customer now?
Jake (SRE): short term: 1) request a temporary burst increase for acct-acmepay (we can grant +50% for 1 hour). 2) recommend smoothing the job (concurrency 4-6) or use our batch endpoint which supports queued parallelism. I'll open an internal escalation to grant the hour burst.
Alex W: please include the exact token budget numbers and which guard triggered so billing can approve.
Jake (SRE): internal note we will include: observed 5-min aggregate tokens = 18,200 (limit+burst window capacity = 14,000), guard fired = route_burst_guard_v2.
Billing Ops: approving temporary +50% burst for 1 hour for acct-acmepay. Ticket #INC-2234.
support-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2234 by Maya. Assigned to SRE Jake.
AcmePay Admin: thanks — we'll throttle concurrency for the next run and report back. Any post-mortem notes we should follow?
Jake (SRE): follow-up actions: 1) add a dashboard card showing per-client burst-token headroom with alert when headroom < 10% for 10m. 2) add route_label model and client_id to existing throttle alerts so we can auto-notify the customer's support channel. 3) add remediation playbook link to the alert.
Maya (support): wording suggestion for customer email: "We observed a short burst that exceeded your configured burst allowance. We've temporarily increased your burst capacity for 1 hour while you smooth the job. To avoid future 429s, please reduce concurrent workers or use our batch endpoint. We can also schedule a dedicated window for large re-scores."
Alex W: also create a follow-up to evaluate whether gptx-13b-quant should be exempt from route-level burst gating for enterprise customers on Pro+ plans.
Jake (SRE): logging the follow-up RFC: RFC-578: "Burst policy exemptions & observability improvements" — will include sample queries: 
```
# Prometheus-style example
sum(rate(redwood_requests_tokens_emitted_total{client_id="acct-acmepay"}[1m])) by (route)

# headroom calc
limit_per_minute - sum(rate(redwood_requests_tokens_emitted_total{client_id="acct-acmepay"}[5m]))
```
Maya (support): closing loop — Acme reports no 429s after we approved the burst and they dropped concurrency. I'll mark thread resolved in the ticket after 24h stable. :thumbsup:
Alex W: thanks all. Recommend we push a small doc in support-knowledge: "How to attribute throttles — dashboards & quick playbook"
Jake (SRE): I'll own the doc and the dashboard change.
support-bot: Incident INC-2234 updated: status=resolved by Jake.
Maya (support): closing thread.
